task_instance: Apply the audit-integrity framework's 7 components to a minimal real security review: created a 36-line vulnerable Flask app (sample_app/app.py) containing SQL injection, OS command injection, eval-based code execution, a hardcoded secret, and Flask debug mode enabled; ran the Clarification Protocol, an evidence-cited initial vulnerability scan, a Retry Protocol against a simulated transient tool failure, a Self-Critique Loop that corrected one finding's severity with documented justification, a Self-Reflection Quality Gate scoring all 5 categories >=8, and a Self-Learning System lesson persisted to memory/lessons.md.
evidence: Created /tmp/.../exec_ext/github__awesome-copilot__audit-integrity/sample_app/app.py with 3 injectable sinks (lines 13-14 SQLi, line 26 shell=True command injection, line 33 eval), a hardcoded secret (line 7), and debug=True (line 36). Ran `grep -n "shell=True\|eval(\|% username\|SECRET_KEY\|execute(query)" sample_app/app.py` to collect evidence for the initial pass. Simulated and exercised the Retry Protocol: a first scan attempt was made to fail deliberately (exit 1), then retried once per the protocol and succeeded (output: `2`). Wrote SECURITY_AUDIT.md documenting all 6 applicable steps of the Execution Flow (Clarification Protocol -> findings table with file:line evidence -> Self-Critique Loop that downgraded the SECRET_KEY finding from Critical to High with explicit reasoning -> Retry Protocol log -> Non-Negotiable Behaviors compliance check -> Self-Reflection Quality Gate with 5 scored categories, all >=8, gate passed) and an explicit stated gap (no SCA performed, no dependency manifest present). Wrote memory/lessons.md recording a persisted Self-Learning lesson (methodology gap: hardcoded-secret pattern matches need a reachability/usage check before severity assignment). Verified the deliverable by re-reading sample_app/app.py at every cited line number (13,14,26,33,7,36) with `sed -n` and confirming each matches the code quoted in SECURITY_AUDIT.md exactly, and by listing the produced file tree (SECURITY_AUDIT.md, memory/lessons.md, sample_app/app.py). No missing tools, credentials, network access, or connector/MCP calls were required at any point; the entire skill (a prompt/process-discipline framework layered on ordinary file and shell tools) was executed with only Bash and file writes.
